level1.name: Foreign Relations & Diplomacy
level1.definition: Conduct of relations with other nations: treaties, diplomacy, neutrality, alliances, hemispheric and great-power policy, foreign aid, and international organizations.

level1.name: War & Military Affairs
level1.definition: The waging of wars and military campaigns, reports on operations, and the raising, equipping, and honoring of the armed forces and veterans.

level1.name: Money, Banking & Currency
level1.definition: Monetary policy, coinage and the mint, specie, paper currency, the gold standard, national and state banks, and financial crises.

level1.name: Trade, Commerce & Tariffs
level1.definition: Regulation of foreign and interstate commerce, tariffs, reciprocity, navigation laws, and control of corporate monopoly.

level1.name: Public Finance & Taxation
level1.definition: Government revenue, the public debt, appropriations, taxes, budgets, deficits, and federal spending.

level1.name: Economy, Labor & Social Welfare
level1.definition: The general economic condition, employment, wages and labor relations, poverty and welfare, health and old-age security, and prosperity of ordinary Americans.

level1.name: Agriculture, Land & Environment
level1.definition: Farming and farm prices, disposal and settlement of public lands, and conservation of natural resources and the environment.

level1.name: Infrastructure & Internal Improvements
level1.definition: Federal support for roads, canals, harbors, energy, and other public works and large-scale national development projects.

level1.name: Civil Rights & Immigration
level1.definition: Slavery and emancipation, racial equality and voting rights, discrimination, and the admission and treatment of immigrants.

level1.name: Indian & Tribal Affairs
level1.definition: Relations with Indian tribes: treaties, hostilities, removal, reservations, allotment, and efforts at assimilation.

level1.name: Law, Crime & Justice
level1.definition: Enforcement of federal law, suppression of insurrection, crime and courts, and morals legislation in the Territories.

level1.name: Constitutional Order & Governance
level1.definition: The constitutional structure of the government: federalism and union, executive power, civil-service reform, territorial organization and statehood, and the integrity of elections.

level1.name: Ceremonial & Commemorative Address
level1.definition: Non-policy ceremonial speech: eulogies, tributes to founders and heroes, anniversary commemorations, and national mourning.

level1.name: Personal Narrative & Reflection
level1.definition: Non-policy personal speech: the president's humility about office, autobiographical storytelling, humor, and boasting of achievements.

level1.name: Procedural & Administrative
level1.definition: Non-policy housekeeping: routine departmental reports, postal operations, and the mechanics of executive-legislative business.

level1.name: Faith & National Values
level1.definition: Non-policy appeals to Providence, faith, patriotism, civic ideals, and the shared moral character of the nation.

level1.name: Partisan & Media Combat
level1.definition: Non-policy political combat: attacks on opponents and parties, campaign debate, press-conference exchanges, and clashes with the media.

level2.name: Neutral Rights & Maritime Depredations
level2.definition: Protests against violations of American neutral commerce and the impressment of seamen by European belligerents during the era of the Napoleonic wars.
level2.era_note: Central from the neutrality of the 1790s through the run-up to the War of 1812.

level2.name: Treaties, Diplomacy & International Arbitration
level2.definition: General conduct of foreign intercourse through treaties, conventions, boundary commissions, recognition of new states, and peaceful settlement of disputes by arbitration.
level2.era_note: A continuous thread across the whole period.

level2.name: Relations with Spain, Mexico & Territorial Claims
level2.definition: Boundary disputes, treaties, spoliation claims, and grievances with Spain and Mexico over Florida, Texas, and other borderlands.
level2.era_note: Prominent from the early republic through the Mexican War era.

level2.name: Monroe Doctrine & Latin American Policy
level2.definition: Assertion of hemispheric primacy and non-interference, sympathy for and relations with Latin American republics, and intervention in the Western Hemisphere.
level2.era_note: From recognition of the South American republics onward.

level2.name: Cold War & Great-Power Rivalry
level2.definition: The global contest with Soviet and Chinese communism and later confrontation and negotiation with great-power rivals and rogue regimes over security and influence.
level2.era_note: Dominant from the mid-1940s through the present.

level2.name: Nuclear Weapons & Arms Control
level2.definition: The danger of nuclear war and fallout, superpower vulnerability, and efforts to limit or reduce nuclear arms through negotiation and treaties.
level2.era_note: Emerges in the atomic age of the 1950s and continues.

level2.name: Middle East & Israel
level2.definition: U.S. commitment to Israel's security, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, and pursuit of Arab-Israeli peace and regional diplomacy.
level2.era_note: A recurring concern from the mid-twentieth century onward.

level2.name: World Order, Foreign Aid & Democracy Promotion
level2.definition: The United Nations and international order, economic assistance to developing nations, and the conviction that America should spread liberty and democracy abroad.
level2.era_note: Chiefly a post-World War II theme.

level2.name: Military Preparedness, Armed Forces & Veterans
level2.definition: Organizing and equipping the militia, army, and navy, fortifications and armament, readiness in peacetime, and the care and honoring of veterans and service members.
level2.era_note: A continuous concern across the whole period.

level2.name: Early Naval Wars: Barbary & the War of 1812
level2.definition: Naval operations against the Barbary powers and the conduct of the War of 1812 with Britain, including maritime independence and honorable peace.
level2.era_note: Confined to the early nineteenth century.

level2.name: Mexican War
level2.definition: The military conflict with Mexico, its justification through claims and annexation, and the conduct and settlement of the war.
level2.era_note: Mid-1840s through the treaty of peace.

level2.name: World War I Mobilization & War Aims
level2.definition: America's entry into the European war, the draft and supply machinery, and the assertion of unselfish national ideals and purposes.
level2.era_note: The years of the First World War.

level2.name: World War II Military Operations
level2.definition: Reports on the progress of the Second World War, battles in the Pacific and Europe, casualties, and the strategy of defeating Germany and Japan.
level2.era_note: The years of the Second World War.

level2.name: Vietnam War
level2.definition: Justification of U.S. involvement in South Vietnam, war conduct and troop levels, prisoners, and the search for a negotiated peace.
level2.era_note: Dominant in the 1960s and early 1970s.

level2.name: Iraq, Gulf Wars, the War on Terror & Interventions
level2.definition: Confronting Iraqi aggression and terrorism, combating al Qaeda and weapons of mass destruction, and armed interventions and peacekeeping in trouble spots.
level2.era_note: From the Gulf War era through the war on terror.

level2.name: Coinage, Currency & Specie
level2.definition: The mint and coinage, gold and silver, specie versus paper money, the gold standard, and the free-silver and specie-resumption debates.
level2.era_note: From the founding of the mint through the abandonment of the gold standard.

level2.name: National Bank & Banking Crises
level2.definition: Controversies over a national bank, deposit of public revenues, bank regulation, protection of deposits, and financial panics and revulsions.
level2.era_note: From the Bank War through New Deal banking reform.

level2.name: Tariffs, Reciprocity & Navigation Laws
level2.definition: Import duties and protective tariffs, reciprocal trade and navigation treaties, tonnage, and disputes over trade practices with foreign rivals.
level2.era_note: A continuous commercial theme, from early navigation laws to modern trade disputes.

level2.name: Trusts, Corporations & Antitrust
level2.definition: Concern over concentrated corporate wealth and monopoly and proposals for federal supervision or regulation of interstate business.
level2.era_note: A signature Progressive-era reform concern.

level2.name: Public Debt, Revenue & Treasury Finance
level2.definition: Receipts and expenditures, reduction of the national debt, surplus revenue, and the general fiscal condition of the Treasury.
level2.era_note: A continuous fiscal concern across the whole period.

level2.name: Taxes, Budget Deficits & Federal Spending
level2.definition: Modern fiscal debates over tax cuts and incentives, budget deficits and inflation, spending controls, and balancing the budget.
level2.era_note: A dominant theme of postwar fiscal politics.

level2.name: Great Depression Recovery
level2.definition: Federal and voluntary responses to the economic collapse of the 1930s, including relief, public works, and recovery measures.
level2.era_note: The Depression decade.

level2.name: Labor, Wages & Working Conditions
level2.definition: Relations between labor and capital, the right to organize, wages and labor legislation, child labor, and urban tenement and social-welfare reform.
level2.era_note: From Progressive-era reform onward.

level2.name: Welfare, Poverty & Economic Opportunity
level2.definition: Anti-poverty programs, welfare reform to reward work, the minimum wage, and helping families toward self-sufficiency.
level2.era_note: From the Great Society era onward.

level2.name: Health Care, Medicare & Social Security
level2.definition: Health insurance coverage and costs, Medicare and drug coverage, and the Social Security old-age system.
level2.era_note: A recurring theme from the mid-twentieth century.

level2.name: Prosperity, Jobs & the Middle Class
level2.definition: Assessment of the nation's economic condition and appeals about jobs, growth, and security for working and middle-class families.
level2.era_note: A continuous economic theme across the period.

level2.name: Public Lands & Homestead Settlement
level2.definition: Survey, sale, pricing, preemption, and distribution of public lands, protection of settlers, and operation of the homestead system.
level2.era_note: From Jacksonian land policy through the homestead era.

level2.name: Agriculture & Farm Prices
level2.definition: Development of farming, agricultural research and markets, farm credit and cooperatives, and the economic condition of farmers.
level2.era_note: A continuous concern, especially strong in the early twentieth century.

level2.name: Conservation & the Environment
level2.definition: Conservation of forests, water power, and public resources and later programs to clean the nation's air and water and preserve parklands.
level2.era_note: From the Progressive-era conservation movement onward.

level2.name: Internal Improvements, Energy & Infrastructure
level2.definition: Federal support for roads, canals, harbors, energy production and pipelines, and rebuilding the nation's infrastructure, including constitutional debate over such works.
level2.era_note: From early internal-improvements debates to modern infrastructure and energy policy.

level2.name: Space Exploration
level2.definition: The race to lead in space, the drive to reach the moon, and investment in rockets and satellites in competition with the Soviets.
level2.era_note: Peaks during the Space Race of the 1950s-1970s.

level2.name: Slavery, Emancipation & Sectionalism
level2.definition: Disputes over slavery in the territories and sectional compromise, and the emancipation, colonization, and new civil status of the freedmen.
level2.era_note: From the sectional crisis through the Civil War and emancipation.

level2.name: Reconstruction & Southern Self-Government
level2.definition: Pacification of the former Confederate states, restoration of local self-government, and protection of citizens' rights after the war.
level2.era_note: The Reconstruction era.

level2.name: Chinese Immigration & Exclusion
level2.definition: The character of Chinese immigration and contract labor, registration and passport proposals, race prejudice, and mob violence against Chinese laborers.
level2.era_note: A distinct late-nineteenth-century controversy.

level2.name: Civil Rights, Voting Rights & Discrimination
level2.definition: Federal action to end racial denial of the vote and secure equal rights, combat discrimination, and include the disabled and minorities in American life.
level2.era_note: From the modern civil-rights movement onward.

level2.name: Immigration & Border Security
level2.definition: Welcoming or restricting immigrants, border walls and enforcement, deportation and detention, and framing immigration as a security concern.
level2.era_note: A prominent theme in recent decades.

level2.name: Indian Affairs, Removal & Allotment
level2.definition: Relations with Indian tribes: frontier hostilities and treaties, efforts to 'civilize' them, removal beyond the states, reservation policy, and allotment of lands in severalty.
level2.era_note: A major concern from the founding through the allotment era.

level2.name: Crime, Insurrection & Federal Law Enforcement
level2.definition: Suppression of domestic insurrection and combinations against federal law, and the administration of justice through courts, penitentiaries, and law-enforcement agencies.
level2.era_note: From the Whiskey Rebellion through modern crime and policing debates.

level2.name: Polygamy in the Territories
level2.definition: Legislation aimed at suppressing polygamy and bigamy in Utah and other Territories through marriage records, witness rules, and voting and office restrictions.
level2.era_note: A distinct late-nineteenth-century morals controversy.

level2.name: Constitutional Union & Federalism
level2.definition: Reflections on the constitutional compact, the balance between state sovereignty and federal authority, secession, and preservation of the Union.
level2.era_note: A continuous theme, most intense in the antebellum and Civil War years.

level2.name: Civil Service Reform & the Merit System
level2.definition: Competitive examinations, boards of examiners, merit-based appointment and promotion, and freeing offices from patronage.
level2.era_note: A signature Gilded Age and Progressive reform.

level2.name: Executive Power, Vetoes & the Courts
level2.definition: Assertions of presidential constitutional duties, the veto and removal powers, interbranch relations, and reform of the federal judiciary.
level2.era_note: A recurring constitutional theme, including the 1930s court-packing plan.

level2.name: Territorial Organization, Statehood & Insular Governance
level2.definition: Establishing governments for new territories, fixing boundaries and admitting states, and administering overseas dependencies such as the Philippines, Cuba, and Puerto Rico.
level2.era_note: From territorial expansion through the era of insular empire.

level2.name: Elections & Voting Integrity
level2.definition: Federal supervision of elections and enforcement laws, disputed vote-counting, and modern controversies over voting rights and ballot integrity.
level2.era_note: From Reconstruction-era enforcement to contemporary election disputes.

level2.name: Commemoration, Eulogy & National Mourning
level2.definition: Ceremonial tributes to founders and heroes, eulogies for departed statesmen, anniversary commemorations, and consoling the nation in mourning.
level2.era_note: A continuous ceremonial genre across the whole period.

level2.name: Presidential Humility & Reflection on Office
level2.definition: The chief executive's diffidence about his qualifications, gratitude for public trust, and reflection on entering or leaving the office.
level2.era_note: A continuous rhetorical convention.

level2.name: Personal Narrative, Storytelling & Boasting
level2.definition: Autobiographical accounts of humble origins and family, anecdotes and humor, and self-congratulatory boasting of achievements.
level2.era_note: Present across the period, with boasting especially prominent recently.

level2.name: Executive Departments, Postal & Administrative Housekeeping
level2.definition: Routine departmental reports, statistics, and recommendations, the operation of the Post Office, and other administrative housekeeping of the executive branch.
level2.era_note: A continuous administrative genre, densest in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

level2.name: Providence, Faith & American Ideals
level2.definition: Invocations of Almighty God and Providence, calls for prayer and thanksgiving, and appeals to patriotism, civic ideals, and the shared moral character of the nation.
level2.era_note: A continuous rhetorical convention across the whole period.

level2.name: Partisan Combat, Press Conferences & Media Attacks
level2.definition: Attacks on opponents and parties, campaign debate and defense of one's record, the give-and-take of televised news conferences, and clashes with the press.
level2.era_note: Partisan combat is perennial; press conferences and media attacks intensify in the broadcast age.

prompts.era_system:
You are a historian building a topic taxonomy of U.S. presidential rhetoric, working ONE ERA AT A TIME. You will see paragraphs drawn only from {label}, plus the word-clusters that statistically dominate this era's paragraphs. Propose 8-15 topics that, together, account for what these paragraphs are about.

HARD RULES:
- Derive topics from THESE paragraphs and clusters, not from a general theory of what presidents discuss. If a concern is specific to this era (e.g. tribal-treaty relations, coinage of silver, internal improvements, Reconstruction, polygamy in the Territories), name it specifically rather than folding it into a broad modern bucket.
- Use ONLY concepts available in {label}. Never propose an anachronism (e.g. no 'healthcare policy', 'climate change', or 'cybersecurity' for the 1800s). If the paragraphs are about a period-bound concern, say so plainly.
- Include non-policy topics when the text warrants: ceremonial/commemorative speech, personal narrative, procedural or administrative housekeeping, and appeals to shared values.
- For each topic give a short name, a one-to-two sentence definition, and 2-3 exemplar paragraph ids (the [pNNNN] tags) drawn ONLY from the paragraphs shown. Every exemplar id must be one you were shown.
prompts.merge_system:
You are unifying per-era topic proposals into a single two-level taxonomy of U.S. presidential rhetoric spanning 1789-2026. You are given, for each of nine 30-year eras, that era's proposed topics with definitions and exemplar paragraph ids.

Produce:
- LEVEL 1: ~12-18 broad domains. Most map cleanly onto conventional policy areas (economy, war & military, foreign policy, civil rights, money & banking, trade, agriculture, infrastructure, etc.). CRUCIALLY, include first-class NON-POLICY domains for speech that is not about policy at all: ceremonial/commemorative, personal narrative, procedural/administrative, and values appeal. Mark each domain kind='policy' or kind='non-policy'.
- LEVEL 2: 35-50 specific topics, each assigned to exactly one level-1 parent (by its exact name). This is where period-bound concerns live as DISTINCT entries — Indian/tribal affairs, Reconstruction, coinage/free-silver, internal improvements, civil-service reform, polygamy in the Territories, prohibition, international arbitration, terrorism, etc. Collapse synonyms across eras into one topic; do NOT collapse genuinely distinct period-bound concerns into a broad bucket.

For each level-2 topic: a name, a definition, its level-1 parent name, an era-of-relevance note, and — for CLEARLY period-bound topics only — an era_of_birth and era_of_death (e.g. birth '1860s', death '1890s'); leave both empty strings for topics that persist across the whole range. Carry forward 2-3 exemplar paragraph ids from the era proposals; use ONLY ids that appear in the proposals you were given.

Target 35-50 level-2 topics. Do not exceed 50.
prompts.crosswalk_system: You are building a crosswalk from an existing 16-issue taxonomy to a new corpus-derived two-level taxonomy, so the existing per-issue website pages stay reconstructable. For EACH of the legacy issues listed, name every level-2 topic from the new taxonomy whose paragraphs belong on that issue's page. Every legacy issue must map to at least one level-2 topic. Use ONLY exact level-2 topic names from the taxonomy provided. A new topic may map to more than one legacy issue where the content genuinely overlaps.
prompts.anachronism_system: You are auditing a historical topic taxonomy for anachronism. For each level-2 topic you are given its name, definition, and era-of-relevance note. Flag ONLY topics whose definition relies on a concept that did not exist in the era the topic is assigned to (e.g. a topic scoped to the 1800s whose definition invokes healthcare policy, climate science, or nuclear weapons). Do not flag a topic merely for being broad or persistent. Return an empty list if nothing is anachronistic.
